terms.definition: A collapsed core so dense that inside its boundary even light cannot escape — the final remnant of the heaviest star cores.
terms.function: The last step of stellar collapse.

terms.definition: The spherical boundary around a black hole where escape speed reaches the speed of light; inside it, nothing can ever cross back out.
terms.whereItIs: The apparent black disk of the hole
terms.whyItMatters: It separates the inside of a black hole from everything else in the universe.

terms.definition: The point at the heart of a black hole where the collapsed matter has been crushed down to essentially zero size and infinite density.
terms.function: The ultimate state of the collapsing star core.
terms.whyItMatters: Wrapped by the horizon, it is the boundary of what our physics can describe.

terms.definition: Gas spiraling into a black hole, heated by compression until it glows — the actual fiery ring we see around the dark shadow.
terms.whereItIs: A flat, tilted whirl around the horizon
terms.whyItMatters: It is the main way astronomers spot a black hole from far away.

terms.definition: The thin, bright circle of light: rays from behind the hole bent by gravity to loop around it before heading out to us.
terms.function: Makes a black hole's shadow visible.

terms.definition: The stretching of an object that falls near a black hole when tidal gravity pulls its near side harder than its far side.
terms.function: What happens to matter before it crosses the horizon.
